manual.icraft_music.start.title: Getting started
manual.icraft_music.start.welcome.title: Welcome
manual.icraft_music.start.welcome.1: iCraft is a music player you carry with you. It plays your own music, audiobooks and podcasts, and music discs: on yourself, or through speakers for everybody nearby.
manual.icraft_music.start.welcome.2: Pick a topic on the left. The arrow keys turn the pages, the mouse wheel scrolls.
manual.icraft_music.start.ipod.title: Craft an iPod
manual.icraft_music.start.ipod.1: Right-click to open it. It plays on yourself while it is in your inventory; if it leaves your inventory, the music pauses.
manual.icraft_music.start.wheel.title: The click wheel
manual.icraft_music.start.wheel.1:
§lTop:§r Menu / back
§lLeft / right:§r previous / next, hold to skip 10 s
§lBottom:§r play / pause
§lMiddle:§r select, double-click to mute
manual.icraft_music.start.wheel.2: Scroll over the screen to move through a list, over the wheel to change the volume. Menu > Manual opens this manual.
manual.icraft_music.music.title: Your music
manual.icraft_music.music.folders.title: The music folder
manual.icraft_music.music.folders.1: Put your files into the ipod folder in your game directory:
manual.icraft_music.music.folders.3: Files directly in ipod/music show up as Singles. New files appear the next time you open the iPod.
manual.icraft_music.music.formats.title: Formats and covers
manual.icraft_music.music.formats.1: OGG, MP3, FLAC, WAV and M4A / M4B (AAC or Apple Lossless).
manual.icraft_music.music.formats.2: A cover.png, cover.jpg or folder.jpg in an album folder becomes its cover.
manual.icraft_music.music.books.title: Audiobooks & podcasts
manual.icraft_music.music.books.1: One folder per book or show; each file is a chapter or an episode. A .m4b file shows its own chapters.
manual.icraft_music.music.books.2: They remember where you stopped and open on the chapter you were listening to.
manual.icraft_music.music.search.title: Search & NAS
manual.icraft_music.music.search.1: Menu > Search finds albums, songs, books and episodes while you type.
manual.icraft_music.music.search.2: Music on another drive or a NAS: add its folder in the mod's client config. It then shows up under NAS in the menu. The README explains how.
manual.icraft_music.discs.title: Music discs
manual.icraft_music.discs.load.title: Loading discs
manual.icraft_music.discs.load.1: Pick up a music disc and right-click the iPod in your inventory with it. An iPod holds 32 discs; they are listed under Music. Its tooltip and the Music Discs row show how many are loaded.
manual.icraft_music.discs.load.3: Shift + right-click with the iPod in your hand loads every disc from your inventory at once.
manual.icraft_music.discs.load.2: To take the last disc out: right-click the iPod in your inventory with nothing on the cursor, or Ctrl + right-click with the iPod in your hand.
manual.icraft_music.dock.title: Dock & speakers
manual.icraft_music.dock.dock.title: The docking station
manual.icraft_music.dock.dock.1: Right-click the dock with an iPod to put it in. Right-click with an empty hand to open it, sneak + empty hand to take it out.
manual.icraft_music.dock.owner.title: Your dock
manual.icraft_music.dock.owner.1: Only the player who docked the iPod controls the music, can take the iPod out or break the dock. Everybody near its speakers can listen. If others are listening when you take the iPod out, repeat the click within 3 seconds to confirm.
manual.icraft_music.dock.owner.2: A playing dock shows its song in a small label above it for everybody nearby (Settings > Dock display). Your own files without file sharing only show that you are listening to your own music, never the title.
manual.icraft_music.dock.speakers.title: Adding speakers
manual.icraft_music.dock.speakers.1:
1. Sneak + right-click the dock with your iPod to link it.
2. Right-click speakers with that iPod to add or remove them.
manual.icraft_music.dock.speakers.2: Up to 4 speakers, within 32 blocks of the dock. A speaker can be heard about 32 blocks away. Without speakers, the dock plays on yourself.
manual.icraft_music.dock.wall.title: Speaker wall
manual.icraft_music.dock.wall.1: 8 speakers, 2 wide and 4 tall, all facing the same way. A chime plays when it is complete.
manual.icraft_music.dock.wall.2: A wall carries twice as far (about 64 blocks) and counts as one speaker for the dock.
manual.icraft_music.dock.stereo.title: Stereo
manual.icraft_music.dock.stereo.1: Stand in front of the dock: speakers to its left play the left channel, speakers to its right the right one. A speaker in the middle plays both, and so do all speakers if they stand on one side.
manual.icraft_music.dock.stereo.2: §lTip:§r for the best stereo, turn on Directional Audio in Options > Music & Sounds and wear headphones.
manual.icraft_music.multiplayer.title: Multiplayer
manual.icraft_music.multiplayer.listen.1: Everybody near a dock's speakers hears it and joins the song where it is. An iPod in your inventory is only ever heard by you; others only see headphones on your head while it plays (hide them in Settings > Headphones). The panel in the bottom-right corner shows what it plays and whose dock it is.
manual.icraft_music.multiplayer.listen.2: Double-click the middle button to mute that iPod (or its dock) just for you, or press %s to mute everything. The music keeps going; do it again to listen.
manual.icraft_music.multiplayer.share.1: Music discs play for everybody. Your own files only do if the server allows file sharing: they are then copied to the server and to the players near your dock. While a file downloads, the panel in the bottom-right corner shows how far it is.
manual.icraft_music.settings.title: Keys & settings
manual.icraft_music.settings.keys.title: Keys
manual.icraft_music.settings.keys.1:
§l%s§r play / pause
§l%s§r next
§l%s§r previous
§l%s§r mute / unmute everything
manual.icraft_music.settings.keys.2: They work without opening the iPod. Change them in Options > Controls, under iCraft.
manual.icraft_music.settings.ipod.title: iPod settings
manual.icraft_music.settings.ipod.1: Menu > Settings: Shuffle, Repeat (off / list / one), Bass Boost, World sounds, Stereo speakers, Mute game music, Shared downloads, Dock display and Headphones. Bass Boost and World sounds only change what you hear; World sounds makes blocks, steps, mobs, weather, jukeboxes and other docks quieter while music plays on yourself.
manual.icraft_music.settings.ipod.2: The last row, Reset to defaults, asks first and then sets every setting back (not the volume).
manual.icraft_music.settings.colours.1: Craft an iPod together with a dye to change its colour. Its discs, link and name stay.
